description: Student team passionate about Earth observation, agriculture, data science, AI, and technology, using NASA data to explore practical and adaptive farming solutions. 🌍🌱
summary:
LEAF is a farming decision-support prototype that helps users explore agricultural conditions based on their land’s location. It brings together climate data, crop information, visual analysis, and report generation to make complex information easier to understand.

Our goal is to help farmers compare crop and rotation options and understand climate-related risks. The project combines NASA meteorological data with agricultural resources to connect environmental conditions with practical farming decisions.

LEAF focuses on accessible information, with particular attention to the needs of farmers in Morocco.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Choosing what to grow requires more than knowing a crop’s name. Farmers need to understand whether their land’s environmental conditions match the crop’s requirements and how climate variability could affect it. This information is often scattered across technical datasets and separate tools.

Farmers also need practical support after choosing a crop, including monitoring plant health and organizing daily agricultural tasks.

OUR SOLUTION

LEAF — Land & Earth Analytics for Farming — is a farming decision-support prototype that helps farmers explore several crop options for their land.

The platform combines FAO agricultural resources, crop-specific environmental requirements, and NASA climate data. It helps users understand why a crop may be suitable, compare alternatives, and identify environmental conditions that require attention.

LEAF also includes AI-assisted plant-photo analysis, a task-planning area, and report generation to support the farmer’s wider workflow.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Location-based crop suggestions

The user provides the location of their land. LEAF uses agricultural information from FAO resources, including GAEZ and ECOCROP, to support the identification of several potentially suitable crops.

GAEZ, developed by FAO and IIASA, provides land suitability and agricultural production potential information. ECOCROP provides crop-specific records describing environmental requirements, including temperature, rainfall, and soil characteristics.

These resources help connect the conditions of a location with the requirements of different crops.

  1. Climate analysis and calculated indicators

LEAF complements crop suggestions with environmental analysis using NASA data, including NASA POWER for meteorological variables and GPM for precipitation analysis.

Our modules examine temperature, humidity, precipitation, and wind. Calculated indicators describe environmental variability and help users assess the climatic context of the suggested crops.

For example, temperature variability helps users understand whether conditions are relatively consistent or subject to larger fluctuations. The wind module examines ten years of historical wind-speed data and calculates a stability index, with charts showing historical patterns.

The purpose is to help farmers assess whether local conditions support a proposed crop and understand potential risks. A stable climate variable alone does not establish crop suitability: its values must also be considered alongside the crop’s requirements.

  1. Crop comparison and planning

Users can explore several crop options rather than receive a single unexplained recommendation. Crop information and climate indicators support comparisons and the exploration of rotation strategies.

Visualizations and explanations make the results easier to understand, while report generation allows users to keep and review their analysis.

  1. AI-assisted plant-photo analysis

The farmer takes or uploads a photo of a plant. The AI-assisted analysis feature uses Google Gemini to examine the image and provide an explanation of visible symptoms or possible plant-health issues.

This gives users an accessible first assessment without requiring them to describe the problem in technical terms. Image-based results remain preliminary and may require confirmation by an agricultural specialist.

  1. Task planning and reminders

LEAF includes an agenda and to-do list where users can record agricultural activities, assign dates, and organize their work.

Farmers can enter tasks such as watering, planting, inspecting plants, or harvesting. Reminders help them follow their planned activities, with notifications depending on browser permission and the supported notification setup.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The project combines a Python backend, a web frontend, API-based data retrieval, agricultural datasets, environmental analysis modules, visualizations, and report generation.

FAO and IIASA resources support crop information and suitability analysis. NASA data supports climate analysis. Google Gemini supports plant-photo analysis.

API keys are excluded from the public repository for security reasons. Users must supply their own credentials to enable features that require them.

CURRENT LIMITATIONS

LEAF is a prototype. The quality of its results depends on data coverage, spatial resolution, crop information, and the assumptions used in the calculations.

Crop suggestions and climate indicators support informed comparisons; they do not guarantee crop success or yield. Historical variability is not a forecast of future conditions, and plant-photo analysis is not a confirmed diagnosis.

Further evaluation with local measurements, agricultural experts, and farmer feedback will help improve the platform.

FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

We plan to improve local validation, expand crop coverage, strengthen crop and rotation comparisons, and refine reminders and reporting.

We also plan to develop dedicated modes for farmers, students, researchers, and entrepreneurs, with information adapted to each group’s needs.

Another planned feature is ownership-document scanning to support the review of whether submitted land documents correspond to the user and the declared property. This will require appropriate verification procedures and protection of personal information.

Our long-term goal is to make LEAF a practical link between agricultural data, environmental analysis, and everyday farming decisions.
